cells.tense: You are here now, pen in hand, tending what you have cultivated.
cells.act: do the next piece of it in front of the person it is for
cells.ask: A piece of work you'd normally finish alone and pass over quietly — do that one while the person who receives it watches. One time is enough.
cells.core:
You can bring a thing along and hand it over at the right moment, without dragging the ending out or making a show of it. The work gets done and the crop leaves your hands on time. This is care that doesn't exhaust, and a space held without clutching.

What has stayed out of sight is the doing itself. Let the next piece of it happen while the one who receives it can watch — no speech, no bow, just the work visible instead of only the result. Something handed over in private is received. Something handed over where the receiver can see the hand is finished, because now two people know it happened.
cells.sheetLine: Let the work be seen, not only the result.
cells.verb: Tending what grows with patient, decisive care
cells.place: Where things finish and are handed on

cells.tense: You are bracing toward a future that has not been written yet.
cells.act: let the satisfaction of a finished thing land
cells.ask: Sit with something genuinely done — an hour, starting nothing else — and take in whatever it offers.
cells.core:
When this much care runs well, things get brought to completion and then left to be complete. The harvest comes in and is eaten before anyone is out in the field again. That is the version where nothing is lost and nothing is carried that does not need carrying.

The care running past the thing it tends is the bending here. Nothing gets to be finished because the next one is already in your hands before the last one is out of the ground. From the inside that reads as diligence.

But finishing is a real event, and satisfaction is what it feels like once it happens. Stay with something already complete long enough for that to register — no tweaking, no planning past it. The hand that reaches will still reach tomorrow morning.
cells.sheetLine: Let one thing be finished before you reach again.
cells.verb: Tending what grows with patient, decisive care
cells.place: Where things finish and are handed on

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you already.
cells.act: carry on with the version you chose through another week of doubt
cells.ask: Go back to the choice you made when things were clear, and keep at it one more week. No sign, no verdict — another seven days.
cells.core:
Something you tended is not here in the present with you. The cultivation was real and the form was yours, and the finished thing did not get collected. Standing where you are, the whole effort looks like it stopped at the threshold with nobody on the other side of it.

The work of tending does not stop belonging to you just because it went quiet. Take the version you settled on back when it was clear and hold to it another week. You don't need the doubt answered first. You don't need anything to signal that it is still yours. Keep going toward it while the doubt is still there, and find out that it holds anyway.
cells.sheetLine: Keep to the version you chose, doubt and all.
cells.verb: Tending what grows with patient, decisive care
cells.place: Where things finish and are handed on

cells.tense: You are still shaping it while saying the shaping was someone else's.
cells.act: accept the acknowledgment when it comes
cells.ask: When someone thanks you next for a thing you grew and gave them, stay with it. Don't wave it off, don't correct it, don't add names. Take it.
cells.core:
You make something grow, then step out of the frame, then treat the stepping out as the honest account. Asked who did it, you would point at the thing itself, or the season, or whoever else was nearby — and mean it.

Taking thanks is simpler than that. When the next one comes, let it land where it was aimed instead of sliding past. No deflecting, no disclaimer, no list of other people added. You stood behind that work the whole time, and the people it was for can learn that from the fact that you did not move. There is nothing here to explain. You only have to still be standing there when it is said.
cells.sheetLine: Take the thanks where it was aimed.
cells.verb: Tending what grows with patient, decisive care
cells.place: Where things finish and are handed on

A reader could reasonably say their tending is already seen and nothing is hidden. The ask survives being wrong because doing the next piece in front of the person it is for teaches the same thing either way. The sentence that serves the writer more than them is the one about releasing ownership without naming any actual person who receives the thing.
